description:
Umbrella for the version-floor design worked out in design discussion (2026-08-14/15). Two complementary floors, both expressed purely in sequencer-version arithmetic (versions ARE microsecond timestamps; local clocks appear nowhere):

1. WAL trim floor (write side): Demux owns the bucket math and commands deterministic chunk cuts; ShardServers buffer and obey; confirmed cuts drive the per-log trim min. Consumer-driven, FDB pop model adapted to object storage. Cross-epoch routing stability is a non-goal (replay through Demux + deterministic chunking makes chunks identical across replicas and epochs).

2. MVCC window floor (read side): a read version is an implicit fixed-term lease (term = mvcc_window_us, a single epoch-scoped TSL parameter). No registry, no renewal, no tracking — client-side local deadline for fast-fail, server-side floors as the enforcement authority (olivine window rejection; resolver oldest_version abort). Long-running reads escape to immutable object-storage chunks/snapshots (tracked separately as a GitHub feature issue), so the hot window stays fixed.

Design decisions banked:
- All flush/cut/expiry decisions are functions of sequencer versions only.
- Demux broadcasts version-advance on bucket crossings (heartbeats included) so idle shards flush and never pin the floor.
- Per-shard tracked state is a "floor contribution" (oldest-unflushed - 1, or high-water when drained), not "last flushed chunk".
- Identical-chunk convergence across fr>=2 replicas; put_if_not_exists with :already_exists as confirmation.
- Replay routes through Demux; recovery pins the floor until the replayed range re-confirms.
- One W parameter derives olivine window, resolver retention (W + commit-latency margin), chunk grid, and client deadline.

Long-running snapshot reads feature (escape hatch for reads older than W): tracked externally at https://github.com/bedrock-kv/bedrock/issues/115

Design decisions banked (2026-08-15, post-review of PR #117):
- KNOWN-COMMITTED DURABILITY INVARIANT: nothing becomes durable anywhere (chunks, materializer
  databases) unless it is known-committed. KCV is piggybacked on every Log.push (FDB tlog parity);
  the Demux gates cut broadcasts on KCV >= cut. Chunks therefore never contain discarded versions,
  recovery rollback is always pure in-memory pointer discard, and the P4 chunk-cleanup pass is
  deleted rather than fixed. Every log receives every version, so the recovery cut (min newest over
  any surviving majority) is always >= KCV-at-crash — durable state never needs rewinding.
- MATERIALIZERS DO NOT HOLD THE WAL: subscriber floors (the criterion-5(b) interim) are reverted,
  not repaired. Materializers stream from the Demux (snapshot -> ShardServer.pull chunks+buffer ->
  live) and have no data-plane contact with the log; the log's only consumer is its own Demux.
  Version currency for idle shards comes from high-water marks in pull replies, not log heartbeat
  consumption. See bedrock-qzr.4.
- Supersedes in this epic's earlier notes: 'recovery pins the floor until the replayed range
  re-confirms' stands, but via KCV-gated cuts, not chunk cleanup; the WAL floor is object-storage-
  only from the start rather than after an interim.
title: [EPIC] Version floors: WAL tail trimming and MVCC window enforcement
